Subject: Technical deep dive recap — latency & throughput SLOs

Hi Emily / Rajiv —

Thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our call and the action items we discussed so we’re all aligned. Please flag anything I missed or want to tweak.

Summary of pain points
- Intermittent latency spikes (~p95 spikes to 600–900ms) during peak business hours causing degraded UX for triage workflows.
- Throughput variability: baseline bursts to ~150 qps for short windows with sustained periods at ~40–60 qps.
- Tight downstream SLAs: patient triage must show responses within 300ms p95 for single-turn lookups; multi-turn conversational flows can tolerate up to 700ms p95.
- Data residency: logs and audit trails must reside in US region; SOC 2 evidence required for procurement.

Goals discussed
- Target p95 latency: 300ms for single-turn inference at production payload size (avg 512 tokens), with P50 ~80–120ms.
- Sustained throughput target: 100 qps with headroom for 2x burst handled automatically.
- Request-level encryption and audit logs retained 12 months.

Model & workload assumptions
- You mentioned evaluation on an internal model similar to open-llama-13B and an ensemble fallback to a smaller 7B model for cost-sensitive queries. We noted potential quantization (int8) to improve latency.
- Typical payload: 450–600 tokens (prompt + expected response), temperature low (0.0–0.7) for deterministic triage outputs.

Preliminary deployment suggestions (high level)
- Dedicated GPU pool in us-west with autoscaling policy tuned for burst handling; cross-region failover to us-east for DR.
- KV/prefix caching for frequent prompts (estimated 20–30% token reduction on hot paths).
- Two-tier model routing: primary 13B quantized variant + fallback 7B variant for non-critical or bulk operations.

Attachments: I’ve attached a preliminary SLO matrix and sizing estimate (slo_matrix.xlsx, redwood_sizing_estimate.pdf).

Next steps (agreed)
1) Dylan / Mateo to propose detailed topology and kernel/quantization tradeoffs (ETA: Monday).
2) Acme to confirm exact payload sizes for the triage and batch workflows (Emily).
3) Marissa to circulate follow-up with links to SOC 2 evidence and pricing estimate.
4) Schedule a joint deep-dive (engineering + infra) — week of Dec 15.

Thanks — strong alignment overall.

Best,

Hey all —

Following up with a more detailed technical take from today’s notes. I’ve included a suggested deployment topology and some tradeoffs. See attached topology diagram (deployment_topology_diagram.png).

Key technical clarifications
- Target workload: 100 qps sustained at ~512 tokens avg (request+response). For p95=300ms we’re looking at a combination of: quantized kernels (int8), aggressive prefix cache, and continuous batching tuned to keep tail latency low.
- Batching/config: aim for micro-batching window of 8–12ms for CPU/GPU scheduling. That keeps throughput high while limiting additional queuing latency.
- KV cache: if 20–30% of requests share prefixes we can bypass up to ~25% of model steps during generation, materially improving p95. Cache population TTLs should be tuned to workload (suggest 10–15 minutes initially).

Topology recommendation (high level)
- Dedicated pool: 4x A100 equivalent nodes (or 8x smaller GPUs with model sharding) in us-west for steady-state + scaling to 8x during peak bursts.
- Autoscaler policy: target CPU/GPU utilization thresholds + queue-depth triggers for horizontal scale; warm standby capacity for cold-start-sensitive paths.
- Fall back routing: if latency breaches SLO, auto-route non-critical traffic to 7B model variant with lower GPU footprint.
- Observability: token-level breakdowns, per-route p95/p50, KV cache hit rate, and model switch counts.

Tradeoffs / cost notes
- Int8 quantization reduces GPU memory and improves throughput but may require a short accuracy/regression eval pass on your prompt set. We can run a small evaluation harness against a few representative prompts.
- Higher burst capacity (2x sustained) increases monthly reserved costs; we can model a mixed reserved + burst instance approach.

Next steps (technical)
- Mateo & I will produce a sizing + cost table with estimates for both a reserved pool and autoscaling scenario (ETA: EOD Tuesday).
- Emily / Rajiv: please confirm the two representative prompt sets (triage + batch inference) we can use for accuracy/regression tests.

Happy to jump on a screen share to walk the diagram — I can do Wednesday 10–11am PT.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
